/reports/nigeria-north-central-north-wes.title: Nigeria — North-central & North-west — Heavy Rainfall and Flood Flash Report 175 (26 August - 1 September 2024)
/reports/nigeria-north-central-north-wes.summary: Between 27 and 30 August 2024, heavy rainfalls in Benue State caused extensive floodings in Makurdi and Tarka local government areas (LGAs). The floods affected the communities of Behind the Radio Benue in Bar ward, Kighir in Modern Market ward, and Agwan Kabawa in North Bank ward (Makurdi LGA) and Sunshine Secondary School areas in Mchaver Ikyondo ward and Market Square areas in Mbaikyo ward (Tarka LGA). The floods affected 1,487 individuals in 196 households. One injury was also reported.  The affected individuals included 1,051 children, 268 women and 168 men. On 26 and 30 August 2024, heavy rainfalls resulting in floods in the communities of Walawa in Magami ward of Mani LGA and Tigirmis in Dandagoro ward in Batagarawa LGA, all in Katsina State. There were reports of three injuries and one fatality. The flood affected 1,535 individuals in 182 households. The affected individuals included 1,006 children, 297 women and 232 men. Also, between 26 and 31 August 2024, heavy rains led to flooding in the communities of Sabon Unguwa and Sibiri in Bungudu ward of Bungudu LGA, Sabon Gari, Alkalawa, Bakin Tasha, Bakin Marna, Ajiyawa, Jangeru and Shanawa in Shinkafi North ward of Shinkafi LGA, all in Zamfara State. There were reports of 100 injuries and one fatality. The floods affected 5,556 individuals in 1,042 households. The affected individuals included 3,116 children, 1,343 women and 1,097 men.

/reports/nigeria-north-central-north-wes.title: Nigeria — North-central & North-west - Intention Survey (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-north-central-north-wes.summary: The issue of internal displacement in north-west and north-central Nigeria has persisted for over a decade, with a significant population of 1,092,196 people remaining displaced for extended periods. Many of these internally displaced persons (IDPs) still wish to return to their places of origin, stay in their current locations, or relocate to new areas. To better understand the IDPs' preferred durable solutions—whether voluntary return, local integration, or relocation—the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) conducted the Intention Survey (IS). This survey was carried out between April and June 2024, targeting 17,833 internally displaced households across 181 Local Government Areas (LGAs) and 794 wards in ten states in north-west and north-central Nigeria: Benue, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kogi, Nasarawa, Niger, Plateau, Sokoto, and Zamfara. The survey aimed to highlight the aspirations of IDPs regarding their preferred durable solutions over the next 12 months, thereby supporting evidence-based decision-making, policy development, and program planning. A durable solution is achieved when IDPs no longer require specific assistance and protection due to their displacement and can enjoy their rights without discrimination. The survey assessed intentions such as 'return to the place of origin,' 'integrate into the current location,' or 'relocate to a new location' as indicators of the IDPs' preferred solutions.

/reports/nigeria-north-central-zamfara-s.title: Nigeria — North-central — Zamfara State Flash Report 207 (22 May 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-central-zamfara-s.summary: On 19 May 2025, armed bandits attacked the community of Garin Na Gwari Village in Sakajiki ward in Kaura Namoda LGA and Ruggar Baba community in Gwashi ward in Bukkuyum LGA in Zamfara State. The attack aﬀected 1,393 individuals across 262 households and displaced 41 individuals across 22 households to the communities of Zurmi house and Yarima Quarters in S/Baura and S/Mafara ward and Maga in Banko/Maga ward. The aﬀected individuals included 780 children, 482 women, and 131 men, resulting in five injuries and two fatalities. Additionally, on 20 May 2025, rainfall occurred in Gidan Gona Camp of Shinkafi South ward of Shinkafi LGA, leaving shelters flooded, aﬀecting 382 individuals across 72 households. The aﬀected individuals included 213 children, 101 women, and 68 men.

pdf_text.text: Event Overview On 19 May 2025, armed bandits attacked the community of Garin Na Gwari Village in Sakajiki ward in Kaura Namoda LGA and Ruggar Baba community in Gwashi ward in Bukkuyum LGA in Zamfara State. The attack aﬀected 1,393 individuals across 262 households and displaced 41 individuals across 22 households to the communities of Zurmi house and Yarima Quarters in S/Baura and S/Mafara ward and Maga in Banko/Maga ward. The aﬀected individuals included 780 children, 482 women, and 131 men, resulting in five injuries and two fatalities. Additionally, on 20 May 2025, rainfall occurred in Gidan Gona Camp of Shinkafi South ward of Shinkafi LGA, leaving shelters flooded, aﬀecting 382 individuals across 72 households. The aﬀected individuals included 213 children, 101 women, and 68 men. Food, non-food items (NFIs) and shelter were identified as the most prevalent needs. Following these events, DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) field staﬀ conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community and Government/partners, and to enable a targeted response. Nigeria’s north-west zone is aﬄicted with a multi-dimensional crisis. Long-standing tensions between ethnic and religious groups often result in attacks and banditry or hirabah. These attacks involve kidnapping and grand larceny along major highways by criminal groups. /reports/nigeria-north-east-adamawa-and-.title: Nigeria — North-east - Adamawa and Borno State Flash Report (12 January 2024)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-adamawa-and-.summary: On 1 January 2024, a non-state armed group (NSAG) reportedly attacked Gatawarwa Town in the Gatamarwa ward of Chibok LGA in Borno State. The attack affected 114 individuals. As a result of the attack, 12 fatalities and 16 injuries were reported. On 7 January 2024, NSAG reportedly attacked Kwapre in Garaha ward of Hong LGA of Adamawa State. The attack affected 1,952 individuals and displaced 530 individuals to the communities of Thabu and Cross River in Thilbang ward and 1,322 individuals to the communities of Kwabaktina, Kukurpu and Waja in Hong ward of Hong LGA. As a result of the attack, three fatalities and 30 injuries were recorded.

/reports/nigeria-north-east-adamawa-and-.title: Nigeria — North-east Adamawa and Gombe States Flash Report (22 June 2022)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-adamawa-and-.summary: Surging communal violence between ethnic and religious groups, and long-standing conflicts between farming communities and with nomadic herders are prevalent across north-east Nigeria. These conflicts are predominantly centered on disputes over land and cause great insecurity and widespread displacement across the region.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-adamawa-and-.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Jun 06 2022 Jun 11 2022 Activity Mobility Tracking Event Tracking Surging communal violence between ethnic and religious groups, and long-standing conflicts between farming communities and with nomadic herders are prevalent across north-east Nigeria. These conflicts are predominantly centered on disputes over land and cause great insecurity and widespread displacement across the region. In the state of Adamawa, between 06 to 09 June 2022, a series of clashes between neighbouring Dumna Ward (Boshikiri communities) in Guyuk LGA, and Lafiya Ward (Kupte, Wuro Mallam Isa and Tudun Wada communities) in Lamurde LGA in were reported. These clashes have led to new situations of forced displacement. Following these events, rapid assessments were conducted by DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) field staff with the purpose of informing the humanitarian community and government partners, and enable targeted response. Flash reports utilise direct observation and a broad network of key informants to gather representative data and collect information on the number, profile and immediate needs of affected populations. Additionally, on 11 June 2022, another communal clash was reported between the neigbouring Boshikiri community in Guyuk LGA of Adamawa State and the Nyuwar community in Balanga LGA of Gombe State. This is believed to be a spill over from the earlier clash between the Boshikiri community in Guyuk LGA and Kupte, Wuro Mallam Isa and Tudun Wada communities in Lamurde LGA in Adamawa State. As reported by key informants, the cause of these clashes is to be found in disputes over farming land. The latest clashes affected a total of 8,559 individuals in 1,499 households in Lamurde LGA of Adamawa State and Balanga LGA in Gombe State. Some of the residents of these areas fled to temporary camps, others integrated in the local host community. The IDPs who were initially displaced in GDSS camp as a result of the clashes have now moved to the Bapitist Pastor's School in Dumna Ward of Guyuk LGA as school was in session. A total of 258 casualties were recorded and 413 shelters were damaged. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-east-bama-lga-bor.title: Nigeria — North-east Bama LGA Borno State Flash Report (29 July 2022)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-bama-lga-bor.summary: With the onset of the rainy season in Nigeria’s northeastern state of Borno, varying degrees of damages have been reported in multiple locations in the region. Heavy rainfalls, accompanied by strong winds have caused serious damages to shelters and infrastructures. On 27 July  2022, the combination of heavy rainfalls with the opening of a dam gate in Cameroon led to the flooding of the Wajare community and a large segment of Banki camp in Buduwa/Bula Chirabe ward of Bama LGA in Borno State. IOM’s DTM programme carried out an assessment to ascertain the level of damage sustained in the affected camp. Over 7,389 individuals from 2,332 households were displaced from the camp to a less affected part of the host communities in Banki.

The /f_looding aﬀected a total of 345 individuals from 60 households. Among the aﬀected individuals were 223 children, 64 women, and 58 men. Fortunately, no casualties were reported during the incident. The /f_loodwaters forced many residents to /f_lee their homes, seeking refuge in neighbouring villages. The most severely aﬀected structures were block/brick shelters, which are the predominant type of housing in the community. Of these, 15 shelters sustained partial damage, while three were completely destroyed. As of the time of reporting, no formal assistance—humanitarian or governmental—had been provided to those impacted. Following this event, Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) /f_ield staﬀ conducted a rapid assessment and identi/f_ied shelter as the most urgent need among the aﬀected population. Other essential needs included food and non-food items (NFI). The /f_indings from this rapid assessment were aimed at informing humanitarian actors and government partners to help coordinate an eﬀective and targeted response. The north-east region of Nigeria grapples with a deeply intricate displacement crisis exacerbated by both human con/f_lict and environmental factors. /reports/nigeria-north-east-borno-state-.title: Nigeria — North-east — Borno State Flash Report 161 (1 July 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-borno-state-.summary: On 27 June 2025, severe rainfall in Borno State affected multiple communities within the Monguno local government area (LGA), particularly those in the following five sites: Gana Ali Camp, Gardener Low Cost, Government Day Secondary School (GDSS), Government Girls Secondary School (GGSS), and the Veterinary site. The incidents impacted 496 individuals, including 63 men, 89 women, and 344 children across various age groups. The rainfall also resulted in 116 damaged shelters across the five locations. The affected individuals remain in the Monguno LGA, with no observed displacement beyond local government or state boundaries. However, the incident has disrupted daily activities and generated an urgent need for humanitarian assistance. The affected persons are in urgent need of shelter, food and non-food items. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, as well as the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response.

/reports/nigeria-north-east-covid-19-poi.title: Nigeria — North East — COVID-19 Point of Entry Dashboard 74 (9—15 October 2021)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-covid-19-poi.summary: During the COVID-19 pandemic, IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), monitors the movements to and from Nigeria's Adamawa and Borno States in North East Nigeria. Assessments are conducted at Points of Entry located along the border with Cameroon.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-covid-19-poi.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Oct 09 2021 Nov 15 2021 Activity Flow Monitoring Mobility Tracking Points of Entry (PoE) During the COVID-19 pandemic, IOM's Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM), in collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), monitors the movements to and from Nigeria's Adamawa and Borno States in North East Nigeria. Assessments are conducted at Points of Entry located along the border with Cameroon. During the period 09 - 15 October 2021, 280 movements were observed at three Points of Entry in Borno state. Of the total movements recorded, 173 were incoming from the Far North Region in Cameroon and 3 were incoming from Chad Reublic. Additionally, 102 outgoing movements were recorded from Borno State to the Far North Region in Cameroon and 2 outgoing movements to Chad Republic. /reports/nigeria-north-east-displacement.summary: This report presents the results from Round 38 of Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) assessments carried out by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and aims to improve the understanding of the scope of internal displacement, the plight of returnees and the needs of the displacement affected populations in North East Nigeria. The report covers the period from 21 June to 27 July 2021 and reflects the trends from the six states in Nigeria’s North East Geopolitical Zone (Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Yobe).
/reports/nigeria-north-east-displacement.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Jun 21 2021 Jul 27 2021 Activity Mobility Tracking Baseline Assessment This report presents the results from Round 38 of Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) assessments carried out by the International Organization for Migration (IOM) and aims to improve the understanding of the scope of internal displacement, the plight of returnees and the needs of the displacement affected populations in North East Nigeria. The report covers the period from 21 June to 27 July 2021 and reflects the trends from the six states in Nigeria’s North East Geopolitical Zone (Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Yobe). In Round 38, a total of 2,182,613 Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) were identified in 444,781 households. This signifies a decrease of less than 1 per cent (or 8,580 individuals) compared to Round 37 when 2,191,193 IDPs were recorded (May 2021). When comparing the number of IDP individuals during the past year, between Round 38 and Round 33, the number of IDPs in North East Nigeria has increased by almost 3 per cent or 64,063 individuals. Furthermore, a total of 1,918,063 returnees were recorded in the DTM Round 38 assessment. This presents a significant increase of 164,579 individuals or 9 per cent compared to Round 37. During Round 38, IDP assessments were conducted in 2,380 locations, with the purpose of better understanding gaps in services provided and the needs of the affected population. Site assessments included an analysis of sector-wide needs, shelter and non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), food and nutrition, health, education, livelihood, security, communication and protection. This atlas was assessed between January and March 2026 and reflects the number of IDPs from the six states in Nigeria’s north-east geopolitical zone. The zone is the most affected by the conflict and consists of Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Yobe states. In Round 52, 2,368,731 internally displaced persons (IDPs) were identified in 485,418 households and 2,277,331 returnees were identified in 377,480 households. The IDP population included IDPs in camps and camp-like settings (901,499 individuals or 38%), IDPs in host communities (1,349,544 individuals or 57%), and IDPs on pathway to durable solution (117,688 individuals or 5%). The IDPs on pathway to durable solutions are IDPs relocated (45,045 individuals or 2%) and IDPs integrated (72,643 individuals or 3%). The IDP and returnee population represents a slight increase of approximately two per cent (35,541 individuals) and one per cent (24,027 individuals) respectively compared to Round 51 (October 2026). One of the major reasons for the increase in the IDP population is fresh attacks, while the rise in the returnee population is due to improved security in areas of origin. In addition, other reasons could be attributed to natural disaster, seasonal mobility due to farming or in search of safety, security, or better services, etc. During Round 52, IDP and returnee assessment was conducted in 3,218 locations across the six north-east states in Nigeria. The assessed locations included 248 camps and camp-like settlements, 1,810 locations where IDPs live among host communities, 67 sites with relocated IDPs, 238 sites with integrated IDPs and 855 return locations, recorded in March 2026. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The IDP and returnee atlas is the product of the Baseline assessment which gathers data at site/ location level using multiple key informants and direct observations. Interviews are conducted face-to-face by DTM in accessible locations. The atlas provides data on the number of IDPs and returnees at the state, local government area, ward and location levels, their shelter type, the period of displacement, areas of origin for IDPs and areas of last displacement for returnees. The Baseline assessment presents data on the number of individuals and households using either head count, previous registration, official documentation or a demographic calculator based on a sample of assessed IDPs dispersed in host communities, camps or camp-like settings. METHODOLOGY LIMITATIONS • Insecurity remains the major hindrance to DTM assessments in the north-east, limiting the field teams’ access to some locations with returnees and IDPs. • Transportation to many remote and hard-to-reach areas have become more difficult as a result of inflation in the cost of transportation. • Some enumerators experienced hesitance and reluctance from internally displaced populations to cooperate with the surveys as data is collected re

/reports/nigeria-north-east-displacement.title: Nigeria — North-East Displacement Report Round 49 (March 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-displacement.summary: This report, which presents the results from Round 49 of Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) assessments covers the period between October and November 2024 and reflects the trends from the six states in Nigeria’s northeast geopolitical zone. This zone is the most affected by the conflict and consists of the following states: Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Yobe. In Round 49, 2,252,348 IDPs were identified in 465,935 households. This signified a decrease of 0.1 per cent (or 3,247 individuals) compared to Round 48, when 2,255,595 IDPs were recorded (September 2024). In the past 12 months, the number of IDPs in north-east Nigeria has decreased by less than one per cent (or 3,247 individuals). However, since the increase in hostilities around October 2018 (Round 25), the LGAs Kukawa, Kala/Balge and Guzamala in Borno State have been largely inaccessible to humanitarian actors. Given that the number of IDPs has increased since Round 25 despite low levels of accessibility, the actual displacement figures are likely considerably higher. During Round 49, IDP assessments were conducted in 2,254 locations across the six states of north-east Nigeria. The assessed locations included 259 camps and camp-like settlements and 1,995 locations where internally displaced persons lived among host communities. The purpose was to understand better the dynamics and displacement trends in the conflict-affected region. Furthermore, 2,129,325 returnees were recorded in the Round 49 assessment

/reports/nigeria-north-east-fika-and-pot.summary: On 12 January 2024, a non-state armed group (NSAG) carried out attacks in Turmi/Maluri and Dogo Nini wards in Fika and Potiskum LGAs of Yobe State, leading to the displacement of a large number of the affected population. As a result of the attack, a total of 2,866 individuals from 510 households were displaced from their homes forcing them to seek refuge in nearby communities or makeshift shelters. There were four casualties and 43 injuries reported as a result of the attacks.

pdf_text.text: Event Overview Between 22 and 28 April 2025, multiple incidents of violence and /f_ire outbreaks aﬀected several communities in Borno State, aﬀecting 1,104 Individuals. On 26 and 28 April 2025, non-state armed groups attacked the Balangele community in Pulka/Bokko Ward of Gwoza local government area (LGA) and Kwapul community in Chibok Wuntaku Ward of Chibok LGA, respectively. These attacks impacted 116 individuals from 32 households, including 52 children, 29 women, and 35 men, resulting in 10 injuries and 27 fatalities. Between 22 and 28 April 2025, multiple /f_ire outbreaks were reported in Water Board Camp in Monguno Ward, Monguno LGA, and Government Girls’ Secondary School Camp in Mafa ward, Mafa LGA, displacing 961 individuals from 222 households into the host community within the same ward. Among those aﬀected were 533 children, 238 women, and 190 men. Additionally, on 28 April 2025, a bomb explosion was reported in Klagaru Camp of Rann “A” Ward of Kala Balge LGA in Borno State, aﬀecting 27 individuals across 21 households. This incident impacted six children, four women, and 17 men, resulting in 27 fatalities. Of all the needs identi/f_ied, non-food items (NFIs), shelter, food, and health were the most prevalent. Other needs included security, and psychosocial support. Following these events, DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) /f_ield staﬀ conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community and Government/partners, and to enable a targeted response. The north-east region of Nigeria grapples with a deeply intricate displacement crisis exacerbated by both human con/f_lict and environmental factors. The non-state armed groups (NSAGs) perpetuate violence, driving large-scale displacement. /reports/nigeria-north-east-guyuk-and-la.title: Nigeria — North-east Guyuk and Lamurde LGA — (Adamawa State) Flash Report 10 June 2022
/reports/nigeria-north-east-guyuk-and-la.summary: Surging communal violence between ethnic and religious groups, and long-standing conflicts between farming communities and with nomadic herders are prevalent across north-east Nigeria. These conflicts are predominantly centered on disputes over land and cause great insecurity and widespread displacement across the region.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-guyuk-and-la.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Jun 06 2022 Jun 09 2022 Activity Mobility Tracking Event Tracking Surging communal violence between ethnic and religious groups, and long-standing conflicts between farming communities and with nomadic herders are prevalent across north-east Nigeria. These conflicts are predominantly centered on disputes over land and cause great insecurity and widespread displacement across the region. Between 06 to 09 June 2022, a series of clashes between neighbouring Boshikiri community in Guyuk LGA and Kupte, Wuro Mallam Isa and Tudun Wada communities in Lamurde LGA in Adamawa state was reported which led to a wave of population displacement. Following this event, rapid assessments were conducted by DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) field staff with the purpose of informing the humanitarian community and government partners, and enable targeted response. Flash reports utilise direct observation and a broad network of key informants to gather representative data and collect information on the number, profile and immediate needs of affected populations. The latest clash affected a total of 1,300 individuals in 200 households in Lamurde LGA of Adamawa State who were forced to flee their locations of origin into Kupte Primary School camp and Tudun Wada Primary School camp in Lamurde LGA of Adamawa State. A total of 30 casualties were recorded and 70 shelters were damaged. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-east-idp-populati.title: Nigeria — North East — IDP Population Variation Dashboard 38 (June — July 2021)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-idp-populati.summary: In response to the need for accurate and up-to-date information on human mobility and forced displacement in North East Nigeria, IOM activated its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the Government and the humanitarian community with multi-layered data on the numbers, trends, status, locations and needs of populations affected by the on-going conflict in North East Nigeria. Round 38 of assessment was conducted from 21 June to 27 July 2021.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-idp-populati.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Jun 21 2021 Jul 27 2021 Activity Mobility Tracking Baseline Assessment In response to the need for accurate and up-to-date information on human mobility and forced displacement in North East Nigeria, IOM activated its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the Government and the humanitarian community with multi-layered data on the numbers, trends, status, locations and needs of populations affected by the on-going conflict in North East Nigeria. Round 38 of assessment was conducted from 21 June to 27 July 2021. This dashboard presents the LGAs with the largest changes in IDP number (both increases and decreased) identified during Round 38, as well as factors behind these changes. During Round 38, the LGAs which witnessed the largest increases in IDP numbers were Gedam (increase of 6,415 IDPs) and Bama (increase of 4,047 IDPs), while the LGAs which witnessed the largest decreases were Jere (decrease of 12,554 IDPs) and Bade (decrease of 6,130 IDPs). /reports/nigeria-north-east-jere-and-mai.title: Nigeria — North-east Jere and Maiduguri M. C. LGAs Borno State Flash Report (08 July 2022)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-jere-and-mai.summary: With the onset of the rainy season in Nigeria’s northeastern state of Borno, varying degrees of damages have been reported in camps and camp-like settings. Heavy rainfalls, accompanied by strong winds have caused serious damages to IDP shelters and camp infrastructures.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-jere-and-mai.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Jun 29 2022 Jul 05 2022 Activity Mobility Tracking Event Tracking With the onset of the rainy season in Nigeria’s northeastern state of Borno, varying degrees of damages have been reported in camps and camp-like settings. Heavy rainfalls, accompanied by strong winds have caused serious damages to IDP shelters and camp infrastructures. Between 29 June and 05 July 2022, IOM’s DTM programme carried out assessments to ascertain the level of damage sustained in camps and camp-like settings due to heavy windstorms and rainfall. Overall, 2 collective settlements, 1 host community location and 3 camps in Maiduguri M.C, and Jere LGAs were assessed. The worst-hit of the assessed sites was Faria Gidan Block IDP Camp, a camp in Old Maiduguri ward of Jere LGA, where a heavy rainstorm damaged 64 shelters, affecting an estimated 350 individuals. In total, 185 shelters were either damaged or flooded by storms, leaving a total of 185 households in immediate need of shelter. There were no casualties reported as a result of the storms. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-east-jere-lga-bor.title: Nigeria — North-east Jere LGA - Borno State Flash Report (2 March 2024)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-jere-lga-bor.summary: On 2 March 2024, a fire broke out in Muna El-Badawy camp in Jere Local Government Area (LGA) of Borno State. The fire damaged and destroyed the shelters and belongings of numerous displaced households. There was a report of one fatality and no injuries reported. The fire impacted 287 emergency shelters, affecting 1,799 individuals in 257 households. The affected individuals included 1,539 children, 131 women and 129 men. Of all the needs identified, food, shelter and non-food items (NFI) were the most prevalent. Other needs included water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and psychosocial support. As a preventive measure against fire outbreaks, most communities need fire-resistant materials for their shelters and detached shelters.

/reports/nigeria-north-east-madagali-lga.title: Nigeria — North-east Madagali LGA, Adamawa State Flash Report (27 June 2022)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-madagali-lga.summary: The lingering conflict in Nigeria's North East Zone has been the major cause of widespread population displacement. Over 2 million persons have been forced to leave their areas of residence in search of safety and security in neighbouring wards and LGAs.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-madagali-lga.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Period Covered Jun 20 2022 Jun 20 2022 Activity Mobility Tracking Event Tracking The lingering conflict in Nigeria's North East Zone has been the major cause of widespread population displacement. Over 2 million persons have been forced to leave their areas of residence in search of safety and security in neighbouring wards and LGAs. On 20 June 2022, a Non-State Armed Group (NSAG) carried out an attack in Madagali ward in Madagali LGA of Adamawa State, leading to a wave of population displacement. Following the attack, a rapid assessment was conducted by DTM field staff with the purpose of informing the humanitarian community and government partners, and enabling targeted response. Flash reports utilise direct observation and a broad network of key informants to gather representative data and collect information on the number, profile and immediate needs of the affected population. As a result of the attack, a total of 665 individuals from 133 households were displaced from their communities in Madagali ward to neighbouring localities within the same ward. The majority of those affected are refugees who are initially displaced from Cameroon. The displaced population is currently residing with residents in the host community and are in need of shelter, NFIs and food. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-east-maiduguri-me.title: Nigeria — North East — Maiduguri Metropolitan Council LGA (Borno State) Flash Report  (03 December 2021)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-maiduguri-me.summary: As part of the IDP relocation programme issued by the Borno State Government (BSG), the IDPs residing in Bakasi Camp were relocated to their LGAs of origin.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-maiduguri-me.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Nov 21 2021 Dec 01 2021 Activity Event Tracking Mobility Tracking As part of the IDP relocation programme issued by the Borno State Government (BSG), the IDPs residing in Bakasi Camp were relocated to their LGAs of origin. On 21 November 2021, the Borno State Government (BSG) commenced the relocation of the IDPs residing in Bakasi Camp, located in Maisandari ward in the MMC LGA of Borno State. Following this event, a rapid assessment was conducted by DTM field staff in order to capture these IDP movements, inform the humanitarian community and enable targeted assistance to the BSG. Flash reports utilise direct observation and a broad network of key informants to gather representative data and collect information on the number, profile and immediate needs of the repatriated population. Between 21 November and 01 December, an estimated number of 4,378 individuals or 769 households were relocated from Bakasi Camp to various locations in the state. Parts of the IDP population organised the relocation themselves, others were assisted by the Borno State Government. Of the total IDP movement, 955 individuals or 161 households relocated to camps or camp-like settings in Gwoza LGA, while 2,029 individuals or 347 households were hosted by the local communities of Gwoza LGA. Camps and camp-like settings in Monguno welcomed a total of 889 individuals in 169 households, while 505 individuals in 92 households are currently hosted by communities in Monguno LGA. Cite as

________________________________________________________________________________________________21 MOBILITY TRACKING — IDP AND RETURNEE ATLAS NIGERIA — NORTH-EAST Round 50 (July 2025) 3 MOBILITY TRACKING — IDP AND RETURNEE ATLAS NIGERIA — NORTH-EAST Round 50 (July 2025) 4 The report presents the results from Round 50 of the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) assessments carried out by the International Organization for Migration (IOM), which aims to improve and better understand the dynamics and trend of internal displacement in the north-east of Nigeria, a region particularly affected by conflict. This atlas was assessed between February and April 2025 and reflects the number of internally displaced persons (IDPs) from the six states in the north-east (Adamawa, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Taraba and Y obe states). In Round 50, 2,292,477 IDPs were identified in 475,234 households and 2,189,318 returnees were identified in 361,953 households. The IDP population included IDPs in camps and camp-like settings (955,135 individuals or 41%), IDPs in host communities (1,234,898 individuals or 54%), and IDPs on a durable solution pathway (102,444 individuals or 5%). The IDPs on pathway to durable solutions are IDPs relocated (40,887 individuals or 2%) and IDPs integrated (61,557 individuals or 3%). The IDP and returnee population recorded a slight increase of approximately 2 per cent (40,129 indi- viduals) and 3 per cent (59,993 individuals) respectively compared to Round 49 (covering October to November 2024). One of the main reasons for the increase in the IDP population is non-state actors attacks, followed by other factors such as natural disaster, seasonal mobility due to farming, and the search for safety, security, or better services. The rise in the returnee population is due to improved security in areas of origin. During Round 50, the IDP and returnee assessment was conducted in 3,128 locations across the six north-east states in Nigeria. The assessed locations included 248 camps and camp-like settlements, 1,774 locations where IDPs live among host communities, 64 sites with relocated IDPs, 196 sites with integrated IDPs and 846 return locations (as of April 2025). EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The IDP and returnee atlas is the product of the DTM Master list assessment which gathers data at site/location level using multiple key informants and direct observations. Interviews are conducted face-to-face by DTM in accessible locations. The atlas provides data on the number of IDPs and returnees at the state, local government area, ward and location levels, their shelter type, the period of displacement, the areas of origin for IDPs and the areas of last displacement for returnees. The Master list presents data on the number of individuals and households using head count, previous registration, official documentation or a demographic calculator based on a sample of assessed IDPs dispersed in host communities, camps or camp-like settings. METHODOLOGY LIMITATIONS Insecurity remains the major challenge to DTM assessments in the north-east, limiting or preventing access to certain locations. Transportation to many remote and hard-to-reach areas have become more difficult as a result of inflation in the cost of transportation. Some enumerators experienced hesitance and reluctance from internally displaced populations to cooperate with the surveys as data is collected regularly and assistance is limited. The data used for this analysis were estimates obtained through key informant interviews, direct observation and focus group discussions. Thus, to ensure these estimates’ reliability, data collection was performed at the lowest administrative level (site or host community). POPULATION CATEGORY The population categories are defined in this report as follows: • An Internally Displaced Person (IDP) according to DTM, is ‘a person who has been forced to flee or to leave his or her home or place of habitual residence, in particular as a result of, or in order to avoid the effects of armed conflict, situations of generalized violence, violations of human rights or natural or human-made disasters, and who has not crossed an internationally recognized state border.’ • In the context of Nigeria, a returnee is defined by DTM as any former IDP who returned to his or her locality of origin (IDP returnee); or any former refugee who returned to his or her country of origin (returnee from abroad).

/reports/nigeria-north-east-monguno-lga-.title: Nigeria — North-east Monguno LGA - Borno State Flash Report (23 January 2024)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-monguno-lga-.summary: On 22 January 2024, fires broke out in Flutari, Gana Ali, and Water Board camps in Monguno Local Government Area (LGA) of Borno State, which destroyed the shelters and possessions of many Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). Many personal items were lost in the fire, including food ration cards and biometric identification cards. There were no reported injuries or fatalities. The fire destroyed 73 makeshift shelters affecting 287 individuals in 68 households. The affected individuals included 131 children, 88 women and 68 men. The victims need shelter and shelter repair kits, other needs include food and NFIs (non-food items). No assistance has been rendered to the affected population at the time of reporting.

/reports/nigeria-north-east-nigeria-bauc.summary: On 31 July 2025, intense rainfall caused flooding in communities across Dass local government area (LGA) of Bauchi State, impacting 309 individuals from 40 households. Among the affected were 218 children, 49 women, and 42 men. In Bazara community of Bazara Ward, the floods affected 118 individuals across 13 households, leading to the damage of five shelters and the destruction of six shelters. Among the affected in the Bazara community were 83 children, 17 men and 18 women. In Gajiwal community (Bununu South ward), the floods affected 191 individuals from 27 households. The flooding led to the damage of five shelters and the complete destruction of six shelters. The assessment identified food, non-food items (NFIs), water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and health as the priority needs of the affected population.

/reports/nigeria-north-east-site-assessm.summary: In response to the need for accurate and up-to-date information on human mobility and forced displacement in North East Nigeria, IOM activated its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the Government and the humanitarian community with multi-layered data on the numbers, trends, status, locations and needs of populations affected by the on-going conflict in North East Nigeria. Round 38 of assessment was conducted from 21 June to 27 July 2021.
/reports/nigeria-north-east-site-assessm.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, AllUsersInDTMNigeria@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Period Covered Jun 21 2021 Jul 27 2021 Activity Mobility Tracking Baseline Assessment In response to the need for accurate and up-to-date information on human mobility and forced displacement in North East Nigeria, IOM activated its Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) to support the Government and the humanitarian community with multi-layered data on the numbers, trends, status, locations and needs of populations affected by the on-going conflict in North East Nigeria. Round 38 of assessment was conducted from 21 June to 27 July 2021. During Round 38, site assessments were conducted in 2,380 locations. Assessed locations included 309 camps and camp-like settlements as well as 2,071 locations where internally displaced persons were living among host communities (down from 2,089 in Round 37). The purpose was to better understand the gaps in services provided and the needs of the affected population. Site assessments included an analysis of sector-wide needs, shelter and non-food items, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), food and nutrition, health, education, livelihood, security, communication and protection. This dashboard presents key findings from these site assessments. DTM identified 879,400 IDPs living in the 309 assessed sites. 81 per cent of IDPs were women and children. 68% of IDPs cited tarpaulin as the most needed shelter material, while 47% of IDPs cited blanket/mat as the most needed NFI. 13% of IDPs do not have access to regular medication, and 21% of IDPs do not have access to food support. In 86% of the sites surveyed, IDPs cited food as the main unmet need. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-east-song-lga-ada.title: Nigeria — North-east Song LGA Adamawa State Flash Report (19 July 2022)
/reports/nigeria-north-east-song-lga-ada.summary: With the onset of the rainy season in Nigeria’s northeastern state of Adamawa, varying degrees of damages have been reported in multiple locations in the region. Heavy rainfalls, accompanied by strong winds have caused serious damages to shelters and infrastructures. On 17 July  2022, heavy rainfalls in Song LGA in Adamawa State resulted in the flooding of the Loko communities in the ward Song Gari. IOM’s DTM programme carried out assessments to ascertain the level of damage sustained in the affected communities. Over 1,200 individuals from 148 households were displaced from Song Gari Ward in Song LGA to neighbouring wards in the LGAs Gombi, Girei, Maiha and Yola North also situated in Adamawa State.

Heavy rainfalls, accompanied by strong winds have caused serious damages to shelters and infrastructures. On 17 July 2022, heavy rainfalls in Song LGA in Adamawa State resulted in the flooding of the Loko communities in the ward Song Gari. IOM’s DTM programme carried out assessments to ascertain the level of damage sustained in the affected communities. Over 1,200 individuals from 148 households were displaced from Song Gari Ward in Song LGA to neighbouring wards in the LGAs Gombi, Girei, Maiha and Yola North also situated in Adamawa State. An estimated 148 individuals are currently residing in the Secretariat of Song LGA. While others left to stay with relatives in neigbouring LGAs. In total, 100 shelters were either damaged or flooded by storms, leaving a total of 100 households in immediate need of shelter. Four casualties were reported as a result of the storms. The affected population are in need of shelter, shelter repair kits, NFIs and medical services. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-east-sulumri-baki.summary: On 27 March 2022, a fire outbreak was reported at Sulumri Bakin Kwalta Camp in Maiduguri M.C. LGA of Borno State. The fire damaged and destroyed shelters and belongings of numerous IDP households. The fire incident fully destroyed 69 emergency shelter, 14 temporary shelters, affecting a total of 482 individuals in 91 households. The affected individuals included 276 children, 115 women and 91 men. Additionally, four goats died in the fire outbreak and other properties were destroyed. A block of shower and toilets were partially damaged by the fire.

The incident displaced 732 households (4,734 individuals) and resulted in three fatalities and 12 injuries. Among the affected were 2,720 children, 1,038 women, and 976 men. The incident displaced 732 households (4,734 individuals) and resulted in three fatalities and 12 injuries. Among the affected were 2,720 children, 1,038 women, and 976 men. The displaced population moved to neighbouring communities within Gujba LGA, including Katarko and Anguwar Gabar communities, and in Damaturu LGA, including Bayan Tike and Kasaisa villages. The attack resulted in the destruction of 867 shelters and the loss of many household possessions. Of all the needs identified, shelter, water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) were the most prevalent. Other needs included food, non-food items (NFIs), health services, and psychosocial support. Following these events, DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community and government/partners and to enable a targeted response. The north-east region of Nigeria grapples with a deeply intricate displacement crisis exacerbated by both human conflict and environmental factors. The non-state armed groups (NSAGs) perpetuate violence, driving large-scale displacement. The escalation of violence in 2014 triggered a multifaceted humanitarian emergency, leading to mass displacement across the area. Cite as

/reports/nigeria-north-west-kaduna-state.summary: On 25 May 2025, a severe windstorm incident occurred in Kaduna State, affecting residents of Angwan Gobarawa community in Buda ward of Kajuru local government area (LGA).
/reports/nigeria-north-west-kaduna-state.body: Share View all bookmarks Download Share Contact DTM Nigeria, iomnigeriadtm@iom.int Language English Location Nigeria Snapshot Date May 27 2025 Activity Mobility Tracking Event Tracking On 25 May 2025, a severe windstorm incident occurred in Kaduna State, affecting residents of Angwan Gobarawa community in Buda ward of Kajuru local government area (LGA). The windstorm impacted a total of 38 households and 228 individuals, including 108 males and 120 females. Tragically, the incident resulted in two casualties. Additionally, 18 shelters were partially damaged, Residents of the affected community remain within Kajuru LGA, no displacement across LGAs or state boundaries has been observed. However, the situation has significantly disrupted daily life and created an urgent need for humanitarian assistance. Initial needs identified include emergency shelter support, household and non - food items (NFIs), and food assistance. The affected households are currently relying on host communities for support and remain vulnerable to the elements due to the partial shelter damage. Following these events, the DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community and government/partners, and to enable a targeted response. /reports/nigeria-north-west-kaduna-state.summary: Between 10 and 14 July 2025, windstorms and rainfall in Kaduna State affected communities in Giwa, Lare, Makarfi, Soba and Ikara Local Government Areas (LGAs), particularly within: the Yakawada, Giwa, Pan Hauya, and Danmahawayi wards of the Giwa LGA; Saminaka, Abadawa, Lazuru, Lere, Dan Alhaji, Yar Kasuwa, Gure/Kahugu, and Ramin Kura wards of the Lere LGA; Makarfi, Tudun Wada, Gazara, Danguziri, Gimi, Gwanki and Dandamisa wards of the Makarfi LGA; Maigana, Gimba, Soba, Danwata, Rahama, Turawa, Kinkiba and Kwasallo wards of the Soba LGA; Auchan, Rumi, Saulawa, Pala, Ikara, Kuya, Janfala, K/Kogi and Saya-Saya wards of the Ikara LGA. The windstorms and rainfall impacted 6,172 individuals (1,026 households), including 2,710 males and 3,462 females. The incident resulted in six casualties and 864 damaged shelters, affecting the living conditions of all the residents. Residents of the affected communities remain within their respective LGAs, with no displacement to other LGAs or states. The primary needs identified include food, shelter, security, health, and non-food items (NFIs). Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, as well as the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response.

/reports/nigeria-north-west-katsina-stat.title: Nigeria — North-west — Katsina State Flash Report 214 (29 May 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-west-katsina-stat.summary: Between 21 and 23 May 2025, a series of armed attacks were recorded across three local government areas (LGAs) in Katsina State, namely Safana, Dan Musa, and Sabuwa. In Safana LGA, Kukar Samu community in Babban Duhu 'B' ward was attacked, affecting 864 individuals from 128 households. In Dan Musa LGA, Galadima and Rugar Gyada communities in Yan-Tumaki B ward were attacked across two consecutive days, impacting 778 individuals from 110 households. Meanwhile, in Sabuwa LGA, the Tudun Amiru-Burdugau community in Dugun Mu’azu ward was also attacked, affecting 385 individuals from 55 households. These attacks displaced 502 individuals from 66 households who fled the violence to seek safety. Seventeen fatalities were recorded, and 53 others sustained injuries, with extensive damage to 35 shelters. The affected population—comprising 968 men and 1,059 women—urgently needs food, shelter, protection, and medical support. On 22 May 2025, a violent windstorm hit Shimfida community in G/Baure/Mallamawa ward of Jibia LGA. The storm impacted 406 individuals across 57 households, destroying 26 shelters—16 partially and 10 completely. Although no fatalities were recorded, 18 individuals were injured, and affected families remain in urgent need of shelter and relief assistance.

/reports/nigeria-north-west-katsina-stat.title: Nigeria — North-west — Katsina State Flash Report 244 (28 July 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-west-katsina-stat.summary: On 21, 27 and 28 July 2025, armed bandits attacked the communities of Kakumi in Kakumi ward of the Bakori local government area (LGA), Mai ruwa in Mairuwa ward of the Faskari LGA and Yarsanta in Rimaye ward of the Kankia LGA in Katsina State. The attacks affected 9,191 individuals across 1,424 households and displaced 3,730 individuals across 590 households. The displaced persons relocated to neighbouring communities within the affected LGAs. The affected individuals comprised 6,017 children, 1,655 women and 1,519 men, resulting in 43 injuries and 21 fatalities. On 23 July 2025, floods affected the community of Unguwar Yamma in Dandume A ward of the Dandume LGA in Katsina State. The disaster affected 1,888 individuals across 277 households and displaced 233 individuals across 34 households. The displaced persons relocated to Sabon layi community in Dandume ‘B’ ward within the same LGA. The affected individuals comprised 1,182 children, 377 women and 329 men, resulting in two injuries. Security, food, shelter and non-food items (NFIs) were the most prevalent needs identified. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, alongside the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response.

The incident led to widespread damage to homes, shelters, and community infrastructure across host communities. Although all affected individuals remain within their communities, with no displacement to other wards or LGAs, others expressed intentions to relocate to safer areas or return to the location of incident once floodwaters recede. The primary needs identified across all the affected wards include shelter, food, health support, and non-food items (NFIs).

pdf_text.text: Event Overview Between 21 and 26 September 2025, severe /f_looding caused by heavy rainfall and river over/f_lows aﬀected /f_ive local government areas (LGA s) across Jigawa State, including Guri, Kiri Kasamma, Birniwa, Jahun, and Ringim. The incident led to widespread damage to homes, shelters, and community infrastructure across host communities. The flooding impacted 5,878 individuals (1,140 households), comprising 2,972 males and 2,906 females. This includes: 796 individuals (158 households) in Birniwa and 873 individuals (214 households) in Diginsa wards of Birniwa LGA; 285 individuals (51 households) in Guri and 329 individuals (61 households) in Musari wards of Guri LGA; 638 individuals (114 households) in Guaza Tazara and 537 individuals (96 households) in Harbo Sabuwa wards of Jahun LGA; 465 individuals (89 households) in Baturiya and 248 individuals (52 households) in Kirikasama wards of Kirikasama LGA; 426 individuals (76 households) in Dabi, 716 individuals (128 households) in Ringim, and 565 individuals (101 households) in Sintilmawa wards of Ringim LGA. The incident also resulted in 825 damaged shelters and 68 casualties, all injured with no fatalities. Although all affected individuals remain within their communities, with no displacement to other wards or LGAs, others expressed intentions to relocate to safer areas or return to the location of incident once floodwaters recede. The primary needs identified across all the affected wards include shelter, food, health support, and non-food items (NFIs). pdf_text.text: Event Overview On 18 January 2026, an armed attack attributed to non-state armed groups (NSAGs) was reported in Kurmin Wali community, Idon Ward of Kajuru LGA, Kaduna State. The incident affected a total of 882 individuals from 146 households, these included 199 children, 295 women, and 388 men. Among the affected individuals, key informants reported that 156 individuals from 25 households were displaced, fleeing mainly to the neighbouring community including Doka Avong and Idon Hanya in Idan ward of Kajuru LGA. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, alongside the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response. Food, shelter, water, security, psychosocial support and non-food items (NFIs) were the most prevalent needs identified. Nigeria’s north-west region has had long-standing tensions between farmers and herders, as well as ethnic and religious groups, which often lead to conflicts, attacks, and banditry or ‘hirabah’. These incidents involve kidnapping and theft along major highways. The crisis has intensified in recent years, resulting in widespread displacement across the north-west region. Definition of terms: Displaced: People who have left the site of the incident (e.g. their home or community), because of the incident (conflict, disaster, violence, etc.), and are now living elsewhere (Internally Displaced Person). Non-displaced: People who remain at the location after the incident, they did not leave, despite being affected. Affected (total): All individuals impacted by the incident, including both those who were displaced and those who stayed (non-displaced). According to key informants, the attacks affected 693 individuals across 91 households, including 385 children, 169 women, and 139 men. A total of 29 casualties were reported across both incidents, comprising 24 injuries and five fatalities.

According to key informants, the attacks aﬀected 2,723 individuals across 629 households and displaced 1,535 individuals from 218 households, including 697 children, 495 women, and 343 men. Of the displaced population, 1,260 individuals moved from the community of Labo Kankia to the community of Unguwar Malam Tajo in Kurami Yankwani ward of Bakori LGA, 91 individuals moved from Unguwar Rimin Jiruwa to the community of Dogon Kawo in Mahuta C ward, 56 individuals moved from Bokolo to Layin Garkuwa and 49 individuals from Gyazamar to Layin Bege in Dandume A ward, 54 individuals moved from Magaji Wondo Dansuda to Dandume in Dandume B ward and 25 individuals moved from Daddara to Fura Girke in Kusa ward. The incidents also resulted in 39 casualties, comprising 27 injuries and 12 fatalities. Following the incidents, Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) /f_ield staﬀ conducted rapid assessments on 9, 10, 12 and 14 August 2026 to inform the humanitarian community, as well as the government and partners, to enable a more targeted response. /reports/nigeria-north-west-nigeria-kebb.title: Nigeria — North-west Nigeria — Kebbi State Flash Report 271 (22 November 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-west-nigeria-kebb.summary: On 22 November 2025, armed bandits attack was reported in the community of Maga in Danko ward of Danko/Wasagu local government area (LGA) in Kebbi State. This incident affected 548 individuals from 101 households, these included 313 children, 131 women, and 104 men. Key informants reported that 352 individuals from 60 households were displaced from the community of Maga to the community of Daki Takwas in Birnin Tudu ward of Gummi LGA, Zamfara State. Shelter, food, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) and non-food items (NFIs) were the most prevalent needs identified. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, alongside the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response. Nigeria's north-west region is increasingly affected by climate-related disasters, particularly seasonal flooding caused by heavy rainfall and riverbank/dam overflows. Nigeria's north-west region has had long-standing tensions between farmers and herders, as well as ethnic and religious groups, which often lead to conflicts, attacks, and banditry or 'hirabah'. These incidents involve kidnapping and theft along major highways. The crisis has intensified in recent years, resulting in widespread displacement across the north-west region.

pdf_text.text: Event Overview On 19 January 2026, armed attacks perpetrated by Non-State Armed Groups (NSAGs) occurred in Yarkasuwa Magajin Gari community of Isa South Ward of Isa LGA, Sokoto State. The incidents affected a total of 1,074 individuals from 179 households, these included 419 children, 497 women, and 158 men. Key informants reported that all 1,074 individuals from 179 households were displaced to the neighbouring state. The displaced households relocated to Gidan Gona Camp in Shinkafi South Ward of Shinkafi LGA, Zamfara State, where they are currently residing in a camp setting. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform humanitarian actors, government authorities, and partners, thereby enabling a more targeted response. Food, shelter, water, hygiene (WASH) and non-food items (NFIs) were the most prevalent needs identified. Nigeria’s north-west region has had long-standing tensions between farmers and herders, as well as ethnic and religious groups, which often lead to conflicts, attacks, and banditry or ‘hirabah’. These incidents involve kidnapping and theft along major highways. The crisis has intensified in recent years, resulting in widespread displacement across the north-west region. This incident affected 176 individuals from 29 households, this included 81 children, 54 women, and 41 men and displaced 176 individuals from the community of Anka to the community of Sabaru in Zakirai ward of Gabasawa LGA in Kano State. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, alongside the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response. Nigeria's north-west region is increasingly affected by climate-related disasters, particularly seasonal flooding caused by heavy rainfall and riverbank/dam overflows. Equally, the north-west region has had long-standing tensions between farmers and herders, as well as ethnic and religious groups, which often lead to conflicts, attacks, and banditry or ‘hirabah’. These incidents involve kidnapping and theft along major highways. The crisis has intensified in recent years, resulting in widespread displacement across the north-west regions. /reports/nigeria-north-west-nigeria-zamf.title: Nigeria — North-west Nigeria — Zamfara State Flash Report 278 (24 February 2026)
/reports/nigeria-north-west-nigeria-zamf.summary: On 18 and 22 February 2026, armed bandit attacks occurred in Gidan Dan Tani community in Kanwa ward of Zurmi LGA and Dutsin Dan Ajiya community in Barayar Zaki ward of Anka LGA, Zamfara State. According to key informants, the attacks displaced a total of 2,710 individuals from 520 households. The displaced population included 1,516 children, 682 women, and 512 men. In Gidan Dan Tani (Zurmi LGA), 728 individuals were displaced to Bakuso community in S/Baura, S/Mafara ward of Kaura Namoda LGA. In Dutsin Dan Ajiya (Anka LGA), 1,982 individuals were displaced to multiple locations: 810 individuals relocated to Anka Town in Magaji ward (Anka LGA), 97 individuals moved to Barayar Zaki Town in Barayar Zaki ward (Anka LGA), and 1,075 individuals fled to Nasarawa Burkullo Town in Nasarawa ward of Bukkuyum LGA. Overall, 79 casualties were reported as a result of the attacks, including 55 injuries and 24 fatalities. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, alongside the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response.

/reports/nigeria-north-west-nigeria-zamf.summary: On 23 and 24 April 2026, armed bandit attacks occurred in the communities of Kurfan Danya, Faransi and Mai Zogo in Ruwan Jema Ward of Bukkuyum Local Government Area, and Keta in Kwaren Ganuwa Ward of Tsafe Local Government Area, Zamfara State. According to key informants, the attacks displaced 1,174 individuals from 237 households, including 655 children, 299 women, and 220 men. Of the displaced population, 414 individuals moved from Faransi, 325 from Mai Zogo, and 306 from Kurfan Danya to the community of Nasarawa Burkullo in Nasarawa Ward of Bukkuyum LGA, while 129 individuals were displaced from Keta to TsafeTown in Tsafe Ward of Tsafe LGA. A total of 27 casualties were reported, including 18 injuries and nine fatalities.

pdf_text.text: Event Overview On 23 August 2026, an armed banditry and kidnapping incident occurred in Sauna community in Sauna R/Gora ward of Talata Mafara Local Government Area, Zamfara State. According to key informants, the incident displaced 531 individuals from 121 households, including 297 children, 217 adults, and 17 elderly persons. Of the displaced population, 531 individuals moved from Sauna community to Tsakkuwa community in Shiyar Galadima ward of Talata Mafara Local Government Area, where they are currently residing within the host community. A total of nine injuries were reported. Following the incident, Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments on 24 August 2026 to inform the humanitarian community, as well as the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response. Non-food items (NFIs), shelter and food were identified as priority needs. In Nigeria's north-west region, long-standing tensions between farmers and herders, as well as ethnic and religious groups, often lead to conicts, attacks, and banditry or ‘hirabah’. These incidents involve kidnapping and theft along major highways. The crisis has intensied in recent years, resulting in widespread displacement across the north-west regions. /reports/nigeria-north-west-sokoto-state.title: Nigeria — North-west — Sokoto State Flash Report 247 (30 July 2025)
/reports/nigeria-north-west-sokoto-state.summary: On 23 and 25 July 2025, floods and attacks by armed bandits were reported across two Local Government Areas (LGAs) in Sokoto State. The affected communities include Fajaldu, Wababe/Salau wards of the Dange/Shuni LGA and Lambar Tureta ward of the Tureta LGA. The attacks by armed bandits in Dange/Shuni LGA displaced 3,829 individuals (760 households) from the Fajaldu and Wababe/Salau wards; 1,562 individuals were displaced to Dange in Dange/Shuni LGA and 2,267 individuals were displaced to Lambar Tureta in Tureta LGA, all in Sokoto State. Additionally, flooding caused by heavy rainfall impacted 1,154 individuals (189 households), including 457 males and 697 females. The incident resulted in 42 casualties (8 fatalities and 27 injured), and 68 damaged shelters, affecting the living conditions of all the residents. The primary needs identified include food, shelter, and non-food items (NFIs). Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, as well as the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response.

pdf_text.text: Event Overview On 28 May 2025, armed bandits attacked the community of Tabkin Dawaki in Katuru ward of Shinkafi LGA in Zamfara State. The attack aﬀected 459 individuals across 91 households and displaced 25 individuals across 11 households to the Gidan Gona Camp in Shinkafi South ward. The aﬀected individuals included 257 children, 132 women, and 70 men. No casualties were recorded as a result of the incident. Food, non-food items (NFIs), security and shelter were identified as the most prevalent needs. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staﬀ conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community and government/partners, and to enable a targeted response. Nigeria’s north-west zone is aﬄicted with a multi-dimensional crisis. Long-standing tensions between ethnic and religious groups often result in attacks and banditry or hirabah. These attacks involve kidnapping and grand larceny along major highways by criminal groups. During the past years, the crisis accelerated and has resulted in widespread displacement across the north-west region. In addition to conflict-related crises, the region is increasingly aﬀected by climate-related disasters, particularly seasonal flooding caused by incessant heavy rainfall and riverbank/dam overflows. The affected individuals included 159 children, 77 women, and 47 men. No injuries or fatalities were reported. Food, shelter and non-food items (NFIs) were identified as the most prevalent needs. Following these events, the Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) field staff conducted rapid assessments to inform the humanitarian community, alongside the government and partners, and to enable a more targeted response. Nigeria’s north-west zone is a site of ongoing crisis, characterised by long-standing tensions between ethnic and religious groups, often resulting in attacks and banditry or ‘hirabah’. These attacks involve kidnapping and grand larceny along major highways by criminal groups. In recent years, the crisis has accelerated, resulting in widespread displacement across the north-west region. In addition to conflict-related crises, the region is increasingly affected by climate-related disasters, particularly seasonal flooding caused by heavy rainfall and riverbank/dam overflows.

/reports/nigeria-north-westnorth-central.summary: Nigeria's North Central and North West Zones are afflicted with a multidimensional crisis that is rooted in long-standing tensions between ethnic and religious groups and involves attacks by criminal groups and banditry/hirabah (such as kidnapping and grand larceny along major highways). The crisis has accelerated during the past years because of the intensification of a?acks and has resulted in widespread displacement across the region. On the evening of 18 October 2021, Goronyo town in Goronyo LGA was attacked by armed bandits. Following this event, a rapid assessment was conducted by DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) between 18 and 24 October 2021, identifying n estimated number of 389 individuals who were affected by the attack. 336 persons were displaced from Goronyo LGA towards Sokoto North LGA, both located in the state of Sokoto. Of the 336 individuals who were displaced, 104 persons were injured. An estimated 53 individuals lost their lives in the attack.

/reports/nigeria-north-westnorth-central.summary: Nigeria's North Central and North West Zones are afflicted with a multidimensional crisis that is rooted in long-standing tensions between ethnic and religious groups and involves attacks by criminal groups and banditry/hirabah (such as kidnapping and grand larceny along major highways). The crisis has accelerated during the past years because of the intensification of attacks and has resulted in widespread displacement across the region. Between 25 and 31 October 2021, armed clashes between herdsmen and farmers; and bandits and local communities have led to new waves of population displacement. Following these events, rapid assessments were conducted by DTM (Displacement Tracking Matrix) field staff with the purpose of informing the humanitarian community and government partners, and enable targeted response. /reports/nigeria-plateau-intention-surve.title: Nigeria — Plateau - Intention Survey (August 2024)
/reports/nigeria-plateau-intention-surve.summary: To gain insight into the future intentions and aspirations of the IDPs in Plateau State, the DTM surveyed 15 LGAs where IDPs have been located. Out of the total 9,272 displaced households in the state, a sample of 1,326 was interviewed. Of these households, two per cent were residing in camps or camp-like settings, while the overwhelming majority, 98 per cent, were residing within host communities.

/reports/nigeria-socio-economic-survey-a.title: Nigeria — Socio-economic Survey and Facility Mapping in Dauchi Settlement, Adamawa State (September 2024)
/reports/nigeria-socio-economic-survey-a.summary: This report provides an in-depth look at the progress made in supporting the displaced residents of the Dauchi settlement, located in Song local government area, Adamawa State. Dauchi, home to over 200 households, has become a permanent refuge for people who were forced to flee their homes due to the insurgency in north-east Nigeria. Instead of returning to their areas of origin, many displaced persons have chosen to integrate into this local community. Through a detailed survey, this report explores the living conditions and livelihoods of Dauchi’s residents while also assessing the availability of key infrastructure and services, such as health centres, schools, and water sources. In addition, demographic data from registration exercises offers valuable insights into the population’s age and gender distribution, which helps inform future interventions for the community. The findings provide a comprehensive view of Dauchi’s socio-economic landscape and the challenges its residents face, making this report a vital resource for those working to improve conditions and provide long-term solutions for the settlement’s residents.

/reports/nigeria-solution-and-mobility-i.title: Nigeria — Solution and Mobility Index Round 1 — Borno State (September 2025)

APPENDIX III----------------------------------------------------------- TABLE OF CONTENTS 3 4 5 9 16 17 18 19 Solutions & Mobility Index – Borno State Round I | SEPTEMBER 2025 2 Solutions & Mobility Index – Borno State Round I | SEPTEMBER 2025 BORNO STATE INTRODUCTION As of April 2025, 1,749,662 individuals were internally displaced in the Borno State of Nigeria, and 897,714 individuals returned to their locations of origin. The unpredictability of the security crisis in Borno State has left fluid mobility in these areas. This, coupled with the closing of major camps in the state capital (Maiduguri), many IDPs who resided in these camps have now integrated into host communities where they were displaced, some have reintegrated into their local government areas (LGAs) of origin and others have moved to different LGAs for resettlement. To help find durable solutions for internal displacement — whether through return to communities of origin, local integration, or relocation – and to prevent new displacements in the region, it is critical to understand the relative levels of stability in locations hosting returnees or displaced populations. The state government under IDSF project launched the Solution and Mobility Index (SMI) in 2025 to evaluate the stability of areas hosting returnees or displaced populations in Bama, Damboa, Dikwa, Gubio, Jere, Kaga, Konduga, Mafa and Magumeri LGAs of Borno State. The SMI seeks to understand factors influencing a location's stability to identify priority interventions for transition and recovery, to strengthen the resilience and stability in this conflict and displacement-affected region. The Solution and Mobility Index measures perceptions of stability and analyzes factors having a larger impact on the decisions of populations to remain in place or move. The tool is implemented in the Borno State to enable governmental authorities and partners to develop better strategies and to prioritize resources that link humanitarian, recovery, and stabilization approaches. This report presents results from data collection of Solutions and Mobility Index Round I conducted in Nigeria’s Borno State between 14 and 25 September 2025. 1. METHODOLOGY The Solution and Mobility Index (SMI) combines 63 key indicators of stability to estimate a single stability score for each studied locality. These indicators cover four essential themes for stability: • Safety and security; • Livelihoods and basic services; • Social cohesion; • Disaster frequency and level of adaptation (resilience to disasters). The indicators for each of these themes are grouped to create sub-scores to facilitate the comparison of localities by theme (see the appendix for more information on the indicators included in this analysis). Taken together, these indicators highlight areas conducive for sustainable solutions to internal displacement. Three "anchor questions" on the perception of stability in the community (sense of stability, community's future intentions, and trends in the situation) are used to validate the relation between the stability score and the community's perception. To estimate the stability score of a locality, the SMI uses the logistic regression analysis that compares the 63 key stability indicators with the responses to the three perception questions. By using the logistic regression, the relation between these variables is estimated, and the probability (ranging from 0 to 1 and escalated from 0 to 100) of stability in localities is generated. This helps to better understand the areas that require sustainable solutions to improve stability and security in internal displacement. 1.1 Data Collection Overview The Solutions and Mobility Index uses data collected through 70 key informant interviews at the locality level in 68 displacement-affected locations in 9 LGAs across the Borno State in north-east Nigeria. Locations for data collection were selected through a mapping exercise to identify areas where IDPs and returnees are located. (See Appendix for further information.) Multiple key informants were interviewed in each locality, allowing information to be cross-validated. Key informants include community leaders, aid workers, and other community representatives. The key informant method has the advantage of rapidly collecting information from many localities. However, it is an estimated representation of the views of an entire community; hence, the results of the SMI provide community- level information. Moreover, the results of the SMI represent a snapshot of the conditions at a specific period and thus may vary between rounds or change suddenly. Figure 1. Number of locations assessed by the state 4 5 5 6 6 6 9 10 17 Mafa Gubio Magumeri Dikwa Damboa Kaga Bama Jere Konduga 3 BORNO STATE The Solution and Mobility Index aims to inform programmatic interventions that can improve stability at the locality to facilitate durable reintegration of displaced populations in their communities of origin and prevent future forced displacements. The governments (at national, state and LGA levels) of Nigeria and their partners should work closely together to identify localities and develop tailored programmatic interventions to increase stability based on the results of the different stability indicators, particularly with the most influential variables. 2. KEY FINDINGS Security varies across the LGAs The level of security varies across the nine LGAs assessed in Borno State. According to the security situation scores, Konduga (100), Bama (85), and Jere (80) recorded the highest security situation scores, indicating relatively better security conditions, while Damboa (30), Dikwa (40), Mafa (40), and especially Magumeri (0) demonstrated lower scores, suggesting greater security challenges. Gubio (50) and Kaga (60) fall in the mid-range, reflecting moderate security conditions. Overall, the average security score across all nine LGAs is 63, showing significant variation in security levels within the state. Strong association between security and feelings of stability and the intention to leave Higher levels of perceived security are generally associated with feelings of stability and intentions to stay, as opposed to lower levels of perceived security correlate with instability, intentions to leave, and a lack of optimism. Most of the residents in the localities feel stable In 89 per cent of the assessed localities in the listed LGAs of Borno State, key informants reported that residents feel stable and safe, indicating a strong perception of security across most areas. Bama, Dikwa, Gubio, Magumeri, and Mafa LGAs all reported 100 per cent of localities where residents feel stable and secure. In addition, Konduga (88%), Damboa (83%), and Kaga (83%) also showed high proportions of localities with positive safety perceptions, while Jere reported 80 per cent. A smaller share of localities, with 12 per cent in Konduga and 20 per cent in Jere, were described as unstable and unsafe, reflecting pockets of insecurity that key informants noted within the assessment. The Solution and Mobility Index varies highly in Konduga LGA Konduga LGA, having an average SMI score of 73, there is a noticeable variation in stability levels, Dalori Quarters community having a score of 99 and Duwari having a score of 15. This suggests that some localities maintain a high level of stability, while specific areas or communities within the LGA may experience fluctuating SMI scores. High SMI score in Loskuri Ward Loskuri ward in Mafa LGA of Borno State stands out with the highest average SMI score of 98, making it the most stable among all assessed wards. Other wards also demonstrate strong stability levels, including Gubio Town I with a score of 97, Gubio Town II and Kasugula each scoring 95, and Nguda/ Wuyaram with 90. Conversely, lower stability levels are observed in wards such as Bego/Yerwa/Ngurna with an SMI score of 37 and Gongulong with 43, highlighting notable variation in stability conditions across wards in Borno.
